- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially in early forecast periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast slope or add mean-reversion term.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or use lagged momentum decay.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.33), model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.0% buffer below forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply “mean reversion” rule: if 3-day moving average of true prices is rising, forecast should not exceed it by more than 1.5%.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 20-day smoothed history instead of raw 30d forecast.
